newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends sharply mixed, Jan off near limit.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends sharply mixed, Jan off near limit.

text.p: January CME lumber futures tumbled for a near limit loss of $9.70 per thousand board feet and finished sharply lower on housing concerns while bear spreading made for mixed trade in back months, traders said.
January ended down $9.10 at $394.90 per tbf with other months $8.00 up to $7.00 lower. March fell $1.90 to $378.80.
Oriented strand board finished $6.40 per thousand square feet lower to unchanged.
Weakness developed as concern grew that the U.S. housing industry may be starting to show signs of slowing. This added to an already weak tone to cash lumber, traders said.
The National Association of Home Builders reported its Housing Market Index at the slowest level since February which prompted concern over U.S. housing starts, traders said.
Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst, noted that the market broke right about the time that the association's number came out.

"When the National Association of Homebuilders start talking negative about the building industry, there is something going on because they are always trying to be optimistic and this is their number that shows a lot of weakness across the board," Schmaedick said.

The association's Housing Market Index for single-family home sales fell to 54 in November from 59 in October. A Housing Market Index over 50 generally means there are more positive responses received from buyers than negative.
But Schmaedick noted that analysts' estimates are pointing to a slight rise in housing starts during October to 1.443 million units from 1.438 the previous month.
The Commerce Department's U.S. Housing Starts report will be released Tuesday morning.
